Focused capillary-model review: Q8 p3 reread. Stationary rotating liquid obeys dp/dr=rho*omega^2*r; pressure balance against gas with surface tension determines interface curvature. This is ordinary force equilibrium, not an unsupplied Navier-Stokes transient. Slow spin-up is explicitly stipulated. KEEP confirmed.

Focused dielectric review: Q19 p5 and wedge render reopened. With the given linear tensor axes, div(epsilon*grad U)=0 and conducting boundary potentials define the solution; diagonal coordinate scaling reduces it to standard potential mathematics. Energy density is E dot D/2. Symbolic static permittivities retained without assuming optical index equals static epsilon. KEEP confirmed.

Focused source-conflict review: Q20 p6 reread. Conducting contact charge equalization can dissipate electrical energy despite mechanically elastic collision; ordinary electrostatic energy plus momentum and explicit contact approximation suffice. This affects the numerical idealization rather than introducing an outside physical prerequisite. KEEP confirmed, with conflict preserved in source-quality notes.

Normalization and boundary integration diagnose the invalid H^2 application using the printed differential operator. No imported quantum evolution rule. KEEP confirmed; coefficient typo retained.

The angular operator/domain rule is unsupplied. Basic angular-momentum scope covers a substantial opening, but the central explanatory prerequisite remains uncertain. BORDERLINE confirmed.
